FACTUAL MAP — Valeo Catalogue & CMS, price / Programs / override patterns
Repo: `/Users/ritwik/valeo-projects/Admin-Panel/headless-cms-frontend` (HEAD `2a2b744`; another session committed during this read — no pricing code changed, `src/types/index.ts` grew 1738→1744 lines from Health-Team additions only).

# (a) Where price is stored today, by department

**1. Health Products — `Listing.department === "products_devices"`**
- Canonical: `Listing.variants[]: ProductVariant` → `ProductVariant.regionalData[]: RegionalData` → `RegionalData.price: number` (**required**, not optional). Siblings on the same row: `sku`, `zohoId`, `vat?`, `warehouse?`, `warehouseStock?`, `isAvailable`.
- Per-city: `RegionalData.cityPrices?: { cityId: string; price: number }[]` (`src/types/index.ts:708`). **Declared only** — 2 references repo-wide (the type, and `src/lib/schema-map.ts:587` → `catalog_pricing.city_id + catalog_pricing.retail_price`). No editor, no resolver.
- Subscription: `RegionalData.subscriptionPriceWeekly | Monthly | Quarterly | BiAnnual`, reached via `SUB_FREQ_PRICE_KEY: Record<SubscriptionFrequency, keyof RegionalData>` (`src/app/(dashboard)/catalogue/listings/[id]/page.tsx:82-87`). Also `Listing.subscriptionDiscountPct: Partial<Record<SubscriptionFrequency, number>>` and `ProductVariant.subscriptionPlans?: SubscriptionPlan[]` with `SubscriptionPlan.discountPct` / `finalPrice`.
- Compare-at: `ProductVariant.compareAtPriceOverride?: number` — edited **only** in the legacy `/products/[id]` editor (`src/app/(dashboard)/products/[id]/page.tsx:1060`), never in the catalogue listing editor.
- Editor home: section `{ id: "variants", label: "Variants & Pricing" }`, `listings/[id]/page.tsx:588`. Variant validation requires a price per enabled country (`if (!r.price) e.push(\`${r.country} Price\`)`, line 531).

**2. Diagnostics — `department === "diagnostics"`**
- Canonical: `Listing.diagnostics: DiagnosticsConfig` → `.serviceOptions?: DiagnosticsServiceOption[]` → `.pricing: DiagnosticsServicePrice[]`.
- `DiagnosticsServicePrice { country: Country; cityId?: string; price?: number; retailPrice?: number; discountType?: "percent"|"fixed"; discountValue?: number }` (`types/index.ts:435`).
- Resolvers, `src/lib/diagnostics.ts`: `servicePrice(opt, country, cityId?)`, `finalServicePrice(p)`, `withDefaultServiceOptions(cfg)` (always synthesises both kinds — ids `so-standard` / `so-fast`, `standard` active by default, so pricing always has a home).
- Money is explicitly **not** on the slot rows: `DiagnosticsSlotMapping` carries `orderSlaHours`, `coachSlaHours`, `operationsSlaHours`, `defaultLabId`, `reportDaysMin/Max`, `deliveryTimeEn/Ar`, `specialTagEn/Ar` — no price field. Comment on `DiagnosticsConfig.serviceOptions`: "Pricing lives here, not on the slot rows."
- `DiagnosticsConfig.coupleBookingSurcharge?: number` is edited (`src/components/catalogue/DiagnosticsPackageFields.tsx:207`) but read by **no** resolver — `finalServicePrice` ignores it.
- Editor home: `{ id: "dxSlots", label: "Nurse Slots & City Pricing" }` (line 599) → `src/components/catalogue/DiagnosticsSlots.tsx`. Diagnostics **also keeps** the generic Variants & Pricing section (only `tx` removes it).

**3. Treatments — `department === "treatments"`**
- Canonical: `Listing.treatments: TreatmentsConfig` → `.plans?: TreatmentPlan[]` → `TreatmentPlan.pricing: TreatmentPlanPrice[]`.
- `TreatmentPlanPrice { country: Country; cityId?: string; price?: number; compareAtPrice?: number; discountType?: "percent"|"fixed"; discountValue?: number }` (`types/index.ts:290`).
- Resolvers, `src/lib/treatments.ts`: `planPrice(plan, country, cityId?)`, `finalPlanPrice(p, dripSpeed, surcharge)`, `planDiscountPct(p)` (derived vs `compareAtPrice`).
- `TreatmentsConfig.slowDripSurcharge?: number` is added on top by `finalPlanPrice` when `dripSpeed === "slow"` — the only surcharge in the codebase that reaches a price.
- The dosage axis carries **no** money: `TreatmentDosageOption { id, labelEn, labelAr?, volumeMl?, isActive }`; `TreatmentPlan.dosageOptionId?` selects which dose the plan is sold at.
- Editor: the Variants & Pricing section is **removed** for treatments — `...(tx ? [] : [{ id: "variants", … }])` (line 588), with the in-code reason "two homes for the same money".

**4. Doctors & Health Coaches — `department === "consultations"`**
- **No department-specific price structure exists.** `Listing` has no `consultations` field (only `diagnostics?: DiagnosticsConfig` and `treatments?: TreatmentsConfig`). `Practitioner` has no price field. The editor routes these listings to the generic Variants & Pricing → `RegionalData.price`.
- **Nothing is actually priced**: 0 of 135 `DHC_LISTINGS`, 0 of the 25 `consultations` rows in `PACKAGE_LISTINGS`, and the hand-seeded `l-consult` (spreads `listingDefaults()`, so `variants: []`) carry a variant.
- Adjacent scalar on the *buying* listing, not the consultation's own price: `Listing.consultationAddonPrice?: number` + `consultationAddonEnabled?` + `consultationAddonListingId?`.

**5. Home & Personal Care — `department === "home_personal"`**
- Same as consultations: no structure, generic variants route, and 0 of 106 seeded listings carry a variant.
- The only declaration of intent is a boolean: `AttributeKey = "durationPriced"` (exposed via `SubDepartment.attributeKeys` on `sd-home-physio` and `sd-home-care`) and `ListingAttributes.durationPriced?: boolean` — comment "Home & Personal Care (hours × days × weeks)". No hours/days/weeks price structure exists anywhere.

**Seed-data ground truth (all four sources parsed):**
| source | listings | with `variants` | with `diagnostics` | with `treatments` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PACKAGE_LISTINGS` (`catalogue-data-packages.ts`) | 1062 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `DHC_LISTINGS` (`catalogue-data-dhc.ts`) | 135 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `MIGRATED_LISTINGS` (`catalogue-data.ts`) | 356 | 356 | 0 | 0 |
| api.ts literals | 6 (`l-oura4`, `l-blood`, `l-mini-vitd`, `l-iv`, `l-glp1`, `l-consult`) | 1 | 2 | 1 |

`MIGRATED_LISTINGS` departments: `products_devices` 321, `treatments` 35. **All 35 treatments rows carry `variants[].regionalData[].price`, none carries a `treatments` config, all sit on `subDepartmentId: "sd-tx-injection"`** — an id that is referenced but never defined (`MIGRATED_SUBDEPARTMENTS: SubDepartment[] = []`). Since the editor removes the Variants section for `tx`, that money is unreachable in the UI.

**Cross-department satellite money on `Listing`** (each a scalar, none flowing through a resolver): `consultationAddonPrice?`, `giftWrappingPrice?` (no catalogue editor; only `/products/[id]`), `heroDiscountType?: "percentage"|"fixed"` + `heroDiscountValue?`, `pricePerServing?`, `multiBuyTiers?: MultiByTier[]` (`.discountPct`), `frequentlyBought?: { couponDiscount?, discountType? }`, `showCompareAtPrice?`, `priceFloors?: { country; amount }[]`, `discountable?`.

**On `Product` only, not `Listing`**: `Bundle.bundlePriceUae / bundlePriceKsa / bundlePriceQatar / bundlePriceKuwait / bundlePriceOthers` + `compareAtBundlePrice` — five hardcoded country columns; `Listing` has no `bundles` field.

**Partner overlay**: `PartnerAccessEntry.pricing?: PartnerPrice[]`, `PartnerPrice { variantId?; country?; cityId?; price: number; discountType?: "percentage"|"fixed"; discountValue? }`. Note the enum drift: `"percentage"` here and on `PromoBanner` / `heroDiscountType`, versus `"percent"` on `FlashSaleRule`, `DiagnosticsServicePrice`, `TreatmentPlanPrice`.

**VAT** lives in three places: `SubDepartmentCountryConfig.vat` + `vatMode` (per sub-department × country), `RegionalData.vat?` and `ProductVariant.vat` (per variant), `CatalogCountryConfig.isVatExcluded` (boolean per listing × country). `schema-map.ts:571`: `regionalData[].vat` → "NO SCHEMA IN DB".

**Schema-map coverage gap**: `src/lib/schema-map.ts` maps `regionalData[].price`, `cityPrices[]`, `partnerAccess[].pricing[].*` to `catalog_pricing.*`, but has **no row at all** for `DiagnosticsServiceOption.pricing` or `TreatmentPlan.pricing` — the two newer priced units have no declared DB mapping.

# (b) What `src/lib/flash-sales.ts` resolves, and what it does not cover

**Covered (106 lines, 6 exports):**
- `saleState(sale, now = new Date()): FlashSaleState` — `isDraft` → `"draft"`; else `now < startsAt` → `"scheduled"`, `now > endsAt` → `"ended"`, else `"live"`. Nothing stored.
- `listingInSale(l: Pick<Listing,"id"|"tagIds">, sale)` — tag scope: `l.tagIds.includes(sale.tagId)`; listing scope: `sale.listingIds.includes(l.id)`.
- `activeSalesFor(l, sales, now?)` — returns `[]` when `l.discountable === false`; else live-and-in-scope.
- `ruleFor(sale, country): FlashSaleRule | undefined`.
- `effectivePrice(basePrice: number, l, sales, country, now?): { price; sale?; wasFloored }` — percent (`base * (1 - v/100)`) or fixed (`base - v`); floor = `Math.max(...)` of `rule.floorPrice` and `l.priceFloors[country].amount`; picks the **lowest** result across overlapping sales; rounds to 2dp; clamps at 0; returns `basePrice` unchanged when nothing applies.
- `flashSaleGaps(sale, resolvedCount?)` — name, window ordering, scope selected, ≥1 rule, `discountValue !== 0`, percent < 100, `resolvedCount === 0`, landing page present.

**Not covered:**
1. **It cannot find a base price.** `effectivePrice` takes `basePrice: number` as an argument. There is exactly **one** call site in the repo: `src/app/(dashboard)/catalogue/flash-sales/page.tsx:405-407`, with `const base = l.variants?.[0]?.regionalData?.find(r => r.country === "UAE")?.price`. Hardcoded UAE, hardcoded `variants[0]`. `DiagnosticsServiceOption.pricing` and `TreatmentPlan.pricing` are never passed to it from anywhere.
2. **`FlashSale.pricedUnit`** (`"all"|"variant"|"service_option"|"plan"`) is stored, edited (flash-sales page:294), seeded, defaulted (`api.ts:2024`) and audited (`api.ts:2047`) — and read by **no** resolver. `effectivePrice` has no unit parameter.
3. **`stacksWithCoupons`** — identically stored/edited/audited, never read. There is no coupon entity to stack with (`PromoBanner.couponCode` is a free string on a banner).
4. **`FlashSale.timezone` is inert.** `saleState` compares absolute instants; the editor writes `new Date(e.target.value).toISOString()` from a `datetime-local` input, i.e. the wall-clock time is interpreted in the **operator's browser zone**, not the selected `timezone`. Nothing converts between the two.
5. **No city granularity.** `FlashSaleRule { country, discountType, discountValue, floorPrice? }` has no `cityId`, and `effectivePrice` has no `cityId` parameter — while `DiagnosticsServicePrice` and `TreatmentPlanPrice` rows *are* country+city.
6. **No availability check.** `activeSalesFor` consults only `discountable` and scope; `Listing.countryConfig` is never read, so a KSA rule applies to a listing with no KSA `CatalogCountryConfig` row. When `ruleFor` misses, `effectivePrice` returns `basePrice` rather than signalling "not sold here".
7. **`discountable` is the only exclusion axis** — listing-wide boolean. No per-variant, per-plan or per-service-option exclusion; no check of `ListingAttributes.medicineType: MedicineClass`, `isRxRequired`, or sub-department.
8. **No interaction rule with the row-level discounts.** `finalServicePrice` and `finalPlanPrice` already apply `discountType`/`discountValue` from their own price row, and neither calls into flash-sales. Nothing in the codebase decides whether a sale applies before or after the row discount, or against `retailPrice` / `compareAtPrice` (the strike-through in the preview uses `base`, not compare-at).
9. **`flashSaleGaps` never checks priced units.** It validates scope resolves to ≥1 listing, but not that those listings have a priced unit of the selected `pricedUnit`.
10. **Seeded demonstration of the mismatch**: `fs-weekend` (`api.ts:1010-1016`) has `pricedUnit: "service_option"`, `listingIds: ["l-blood","l-mini-vitd"]`. Both are Diagnostics listings with `variants: []`, so the preview row renders literally `no UAE price to show` for the sale whose priced unit is service options.
11. Nothing persists a sale price onto a listing (as designed) — but there is also no read-path function that, given a `Listing`, returns its priced units with a sale applied. That function does not exist for any department.

# (c) "Programs" is four distinct things in the code

**1. `sd-consultations-programs` — a `SubDepartment` row (classification, "what it is")**
Defined in `src/services/catalogue-data-packages.ts` → `PACKAGE_SUBDEPARTMENTS` (16 rows): `{ id: "sd-consultations-programs", department: "consultations", nameEn: "Programs", nameAr: …, slug: "programs", sortOrder, isActive: true, attributeKeys: [] }`. A listing has exactly one `subDepartmentId`.
Carriers: **24 listings, all from `DHC_LISTINGS`** (`pkg-coach-36/37/38/39/42/66/81/83/85/86/87/91/107/109/110/111/113/114/115/116/117/118/120/124`) — all `department: "consultations"`, all `fulfilmentPath: "consultation"`, all `journeyIds: []`, all `subCategoryIds: []`, 21 `active` / 3 `inactive`, none with pricing, `practitionerIds`, or `countryConfig`.
The file header states department/sub-department are generated **proposals**; several rows are plainly consultations rather than programs: "IV Consultation", "Free Peptide Consultation", "Free IV Therapy Consultation", "Repeat Peptide Consultation", "Online Test Results Consultation", "Functional Test consultation", "Shaymaa Badreddine: Dietitian Consultation". `attributeKeys: []` means it exposes no extra fields; the editor gives these the generic Variants & Pricing section.

**2. `TreatmentPlan.kind === "course"` — a priced unit inside one Treatments listing**
`TreatmentPlanKind = "single" | "couple" | "group" | "course"`; `TREATMENT_PLAN_KINDS` labels it **"Multi-session plan"**, blurb "A course of sessions sold together, usually with a coach."
Scope: one row in `listing.treatments.plans[]`. Fields it uses: `sessionCount`, `validityDays`, `includesConsultation`, `flexibleRescheduling`, `coachRecommended`, `clinicianName`, `clinicianRole`, `socialProofCount`, `giftEn`, `benefitsEn[]`, `dosageOptionId`, and **`pricing: TreatmentPlanPrice[]` — it carries money**.
Derived constraints: `flowForSubDepartment(slug)` returns `allowPlans: false` for vaccine slugs; `treatmentsGaps` flags `kind === "course" && !sessionCount`.
Seeded: `tp-advanced` "IV-Advanced Plan" on `l-iv` — 8 sessions / 90 days / UAE 720 vs `compareAtPrice` 1108, KSA 790 vs 1215.
Never crosses listings.

**3. `Journey` with `kind: "program"` — top-level context wrapping many listings**
`interface Journey extends Entity { nameEn; nameAr; slug; kind: "program"|"direct"; isActive; listingIds: string[]; pageBlocks?: PageBlock[]; retention?: JourneyRetention[]; retentionAttachments?: { country: Country; templateId? }[]; partnerAccess?; partnerExclusive? }`.
M:M with listings, from both sides (`Listing.journeyIds` ↔ `Journey.listingIds`). It has **no price field, no country availability, no sub-department, no status beyond `isActive`**. Its money is a display string only: `PageBlockConfig.priceLabel` / `priceLabelAr` ("From AED 899/mo" in `jr-weightloss` block `b1`).
What it owns instead: a block page (`PageBlock[]`, 12 `PageBlockType` values) and per-country retention (`JourneyRetention` legacy 4 fixed slots, or `retentionAttachments` → `RetentionTemplate`).
Seeded: `jr-direct` (`kind: "direct"`, `listingIds: []`), `jr-weightloss` (`program`, `listingIds: ["p1","l-glp1"]`), `jr-longevity` (`program`, `listingIds: ["p2"]`). `"p1"`/`"p2"` are `MOCK_PRODUCTS` ids, not `Listing` ids.
**Not persisted**: `ApiService.catalogue.journeys()` returns a literal through `mockFetch` with no module-level store (unlike `LISTINGS_STORE`, `RETENTION_STORE`, `FLASH_SALES_STORE`, `TAGS_STORE`); the create dialog says "Mock only — not persisted."

**4. `Protocol` — the adjacent fourth thing, explicitly not a Journey kind**
Header comment: "Protocol — clinically-distinct care sequence (NOT a Journey kind)". `Protocol { code; nameEn; nameAr; clinicianAuthor; targetCondition?; journeyId?; status: ProtocolStatus; isActive; steps: ProtocolStep[] }`, `ProtocolStep { order; type: ProtocolStepType; cadence?; dosing?; gating?: ProtocolGating; gatingNote?; linkedListingId? }`. Links *up* to a journey via `journeyId?`. No price.

**The three-way difference, stated as data:**
| | `sd-consultations-programs` | `TreatmentPlan.kind "course"` | `Journey.kind "program"` |
|---|---|---|---|
| entity | `SubDepartment` | row inside `TreatmentsConfig.plans[]` | `Journey` (own entity) |
| taxonomy role | "what it is" (1 per listing) | none — a sellable unit | context wrapper (M:M) |
| cardinality vs listing | 1 sub-dept → N listings | N plans within **1** listing | 1 journey ↔ N listings, N journeys ↔ 1 listing |
| carries price | no | **yes** (`pricing: TreatmentPlanPrice[]`) | no (`priceLabel` string only) |
| session count | not modelled | `sessionCount` + `validityDays` | not modelled |
| persisted in prototype | yes (seed data) | yes (in `LISTINGS_STORE`) | **no** store |
| audit `AuditEntityType` | `"subDepartment"` | none (audited as `"listing"`) | `"journey"` |
| current carriers | 24 listings, none priced | 1 seeded plan (`tp-advanced`) | 2 program journeys |

# (d) Per-country / per-city override patterns already in the code

**Pattern A — row per country with optional `cityId` (three instances, identical shape, two different merge semantics)**
- `DiagnosticsServicePrice` → resolver `servicePrice()` (`src/lib/diagnostics.ts:223-231`): `return { ...(base ?? { country }), ...city }`.
- `TreatmentPlanPrice` → resolver `planPrice()` (`src/lib/treatments.ts:14-22`): identical bare spread.
- `DiagnosticsSlotMapping` → resolver `effectiveSlot()` (`src/lib/diagnostics.ts:133-150`): does **not** rely on the spread. After `{ ...base, ...city }` it loops `Object.keys(city)` and restores `base[k]` wherever the city value is `undefined` — comment "undefined on the city row means 'inherit', not 'zero'" — then forces `merged.id = city.id; merged.cityId = city.cityId`.

Observed behavioural consequence of that difference: both city-price editors write `undefined` as an **own property** when a field is cleared — `TreatmentPlans.tsx:66-73` `setPrice` → `{ ...p, [field]: value }` fed by `Num`'s `onSet(e.target.value === "" ? undefined : Number(...))`, and `DiagnosticsSlots.tsx:64-71` `setPrice` the same. A spread copies own `undefined` properties, so a city row whose price was typed and then cleared overwrites the country `price` with `undefined`, and both `finalPlanPrice` and `finalServicePrice` open with `if (!p || p.price === undefined) return undefined`. A city row created by "Add city" (`{ country, cityId: c.id }` — `TreatmentPlans.tsx:532`, `DiagnosticsSlots.tsx:234`) has no `price` key and does inherit. `DiagnosticsSlots.tsx:108-112` advertises the inheritance in the UI: `placeholder={`inherits ${base.price}`}`.

**Pattern B — country-only row, "no row = not available"**
- `CatalogCountryConfig` on `Listing.countryConfig[]`: `{ country, status, isSubscriptionEnabled, isVatExcluded, isCodEligible, isCouponEligible }`. This is the list every department gate iterates — `diagnosticsGaps` and `treatmentsGaps` both do `(l.countryConfig ?? []).map(c => c.country)` — and what feeds `CountrySwitcher` (`src/components/catalogue/CountrySwitcher.tsx`, one country edited at a time, with an optional per-country badge count).
- `RegionalData` — the Health Products per-country row (country + sku + zohoId + price + vat + warehouse + stock + availability, all in one row).
- `BiomarkerCountryMap { country, biomarkerIds[], nonBiomarkerTestIds?, intentionalNote? }` — country-only by explicit design, with `intentionalNote` as the "this divergence is deliberate" marker that `diagnosticsGaps` reads to downgrade severe drift from a blocker to a recorded decision.
- `SeoCountrySettings { country, isIndexable?, isFollowable?, sitemapInclude?, ogImageUrl?, ogImageAltEn/Ar? }`.
- `FlashSaleRule { country, discountType, discountValue, floorPrice? }`.
- `Listing.priceFloors?: { country: Country; amount: number }[]`.
- `JourneyRetention { country, slots: RetentionSlot[] }` and `Journey.retentionAttachments?: { country, templateId? }[]`.

**Pattern C — country row plus a second, non-geographic exception axis (unique)**
- `SubDepartmentCountryConfig { country, vat?, zohoOrgId?, paymentMethods?, zohoBook?: ZohoBook, invoicingEnabled?, vatMode?: "exclusive"|"inclusive", zohoAccountId?, overrides?: { medicineClass: MedicineClass; zohoBook?; vat?; note? }[] }`. The only place in the model where an override is keyed on a clinical class rather than geography (UAE GLP-1 → `shifa`, zero-rated). Set at `SubDepartment.countryConfig[]`, not per variant.

**Pattern D — three-level inherit (city → country → master), declared and implemented in the UI only**
- `SeoLocaleEntry { id, country, cityId?, language: SeoLang, slug?, metaTitle?, metaDescription?, h1?, canonicalUrl?, deliveryPromise? }`; type comment "Blank field = inherit (city → country → master)"; DB shape `seo_meta` keyed `(entity_id, country_id, language_code)` with city rows as `entity_type='CITY_PAGE'`. There is **no resolver function** — the fallback exists only as `placeholder` strings in `SeoLocalisation.tsx` ("inherits master" at lines 106/115/125, "inherits country" at 289/295/299), and blank means empty string rather than `undefined`.

**Pattern E — declared, no resolver**
- `RegionalData.cityPrices?: { cityId: string; price: number }[]` — type + schema-map only.
- `PartnerPrice { variantId?, country?, cityId?, price, discountType?, discountValue? }` — the only pattern with **three** optional scoping axes (variant / country / city). Edited in `src/components/catalogue/PartnerAccessSection.tsx:168-178` (changing country resets `cityId: undefined`); nothing resolves it into an effective price.

**Non-`cityId` geography already in use**
- `DeliveryConfig { city: string; deliveryTime: string; isAvailable: boolean }` — free-text city **name**, not a `City.id`. `schema-map.ts:361`: "No per-city delivery table; catalog_country_config is country-level only and catalog_pricing.city_id is price-only."
- `SlotGroup.cityId?` — city-scoped in the Order Service (`api/v1/slots/groups?cityId=`); a row with **no** `cityId` is the national fallback (`sg-national-std`), and `DiagnosticsSlots.tsx:392` filters `groups.filter(g => !g.cityId || g.cityId === k.cityId)` with the label suffix `" · national"`. `ApiService.catalogue.slotGroups(cityId?)` mirrors that same "city groups plus national fallback" rule.
- `RegulatorJurisdiction` / `PractitionerLicence.jurisdictionId` — **sub-country** scoping, 6 fixed rows, 3 of them inside the UAE (`ae-dubai`/DHA, `ae-abudhabi`/DoH, `ae-northern`/MOHAP).

**Masters**: `City { id, name, country }` — 7 rows in `ApiService.catalogue.cities()` (`c-dubai`, `c-abudhabi`, `c-sharjah`, `c-riyadh`, `c-jeddah`, `c-doha`, `c-kuwaitcity`). `Country = "UAE"|"KSA"|"QATAR"|"KUWAIT"|"OTHERS"` — 5 values; `OTHERS` has no city and appears in the flash-sales `COUNTRIES` array.

# Cross-check: the activation gate does not know where price lives

`listingActivationRequirements(l)` (`src/lib/catalogue.ts:85-117`) includes, **ungated by department**:
`{ key: "variant", label: "At least one variant with a price", met: hasPricedVariant }` where `hasPricedVariant = (l.variants ?? []).some(v => (v.regionalData ?? []).some(r => (r.price ?? 0) > 0))`, and `{ key: "image", … }` from `mediaGallery` / variant media.
`onStatusChange` hard-blocks the transition: `if (v === "active" && unmetReqs.length > 0) { setActivationOpen(true); return }` (`listings/[id]/page.tsx:647`), and the Published option is `disabled={st.id === "active" && unmetReqs.length > 0}` (line 699).

Observed both directions:
- `l-blood` (priced Standard 899 / Fast Track 1099 UAE via `serviceOptions`) and `l-iv` (four priced plans) both have `variants: []` and `mediaGallery: []` from `listingDefaults()`, so both fail `variant` **and** `image` while seeded `status: "active"`.
- The 35 `sd-tx-injection` treatments listings **pass** the `variant` requirement on `regionalData[].price` — money the editor hides for `tx` — and fail only `image` (0 of 35 have any variant `imageUrl` or listing `mediaGallery`).
- `diagnosticsGaps(l)` and `treatmentsGaps(l)` — which *do* check priced service options and priced plans per enabled country — are wired only to section `hasError` flags and advisory panels (`listings/[id]/page.tsx:575`, 1847, 1883). Their own comments say they are "Deliberately separate from `listingActivationRequirements`" / "Kept out of the generic activation gate", and `unmetReqs` never includes them.

Flash Sales redesign — priced-unit resol.topic: Flash Sales redesign — priced-unit resolution, per-country windows, and the sale/price-change split
Flash Sales redesign — priced-unit resol.recommendation: The current design's principles are right — never write onto a listing, derive state from the window, scope by campaign tag, landing page is a real category page — but its mechanics are unbuilt: `effectivePrice(basePrice: number, …)` cannot find a base price, and `pricedUnit`, `stacksWithCoupons`, `timezone` and `landingCategoryId` are all stored, edited, audited and read by nothing. The fix is one missing abstraction: a `PricedUnit` adapter (`src/lib/priced-units.ts`) that normalises `RegionalData`, `DiagnosticsServiceOption.pricing` and `TreatmentPlan.pricing` into addressable `PricedUnitRef`s, plus a three-number contract per unit — `listPrice` (compare-at anchor), `standingPrice` (permanent price, row discount already inside), `sellingPrice` (standing price with at most one sale) — so a sale never compounds with a row discount and never touches the marketing anchor. Then replace `pricedUnit` with a unit filter plus sale-level `excludedUnitRefs`, replace the single `startsAt/endsAt/timezone` instant with a per-country resolvable window, and split off a `PriceChange` entity for permanent scheduled changes so a forgotten sale can never become the price. Every resolver returns a discriminated `ResolvedPrice` with a step-by-step explanation and a `revalidateAt`, which is what makes ops answerable and the read path cacheable at the same time.

cases.case: Does pricedUnit ('all' | 'variant' | 'service_option' | 'plan') work when a listing has four plans at four prices?
cases.behaviour: No — it is the wrong axis and it is decorative today. It selects a unit TYPE, but the type is already fully determined by the listing's department (established decision 3), so `plan` adds no information the PricedUnit adapter cannot derive; and it cannot express "20% off the single session but not the 8-session course", which is the actual merchandising intent. `pricedUnit` is also read by no resolver anywhere: it is stored, edited (page.tsx:294), defaulted (api.ts:2024) and audited (api.ts:2047), and effectivePrice has no unit parameter. REPLACE with three things: (1) unit identity — every priced unit is addressable as a PricedUnitRef { listingId, kind, unitId }; (2) SaleScope.unitFilter { kinds?, planKinds?, serviceKinds? } for scopes that cannot enumerate units (tag scope), so "single sessions only" or "Fast Track only" is expressible; (3) SaleScope.excludedUnitRefs for named exceptions. Applied to l-iv's four plans: a sale with planKinds: ["single"] prices tp-single only; a sale with no filter prices all four but each against its own standingPrice, so the 8-session course discounts off 720 and not off its 1108 compareAtPrice.

cases.case: What happens with overlapping sales (currently "best price wins")?
cases.behaviour: KEEP best-price-wins as the read-path rule — it is the only outcome that never looks like a bug from outside, and it is deterministic. Never compound: at most ONE sale ever applies to one unit, stated in the type (ResolvedPrice.sale is singular). What is missing is not the resolution rule but three guards. (1) DETECTION at authoring time: flashSaleGaps must list overlapping live/scheduled sales by name with the count of units both touch — today two campaign owners can both hit a listing and nobody is told. (2) A BLOCKER, not an exclusivity flag: I considered `precedence: "exclusive"` and reject it, because two overlapping exclusive sales reintroduce exactly the undefined winner this is meant to fix; instead the overlap gap is a hard blocker that forces the human decision at authoring time. `precedence` is typed as the literal "best_price" so widening it is a reviewable change. (3) FIXED-AMOUNT GUARDS: percent is scale-free, fixed is not — a 200 AED rule aimed at a 1200 plan lands on a 250 supplement and clamps to 0. rule.floorPrice is a single scalar for a whole heterogeneous scope, so it is only meaningful when the scope is homogeneous. Therefore: fixed requires a floorPrice, and fixed on tag scope spanning more than one department is blocked outright.

cases.case: Coupon stacking?
cases.behaviour: `stacksWithCoupons` is a field with no counterparty and must be reframed, not kept. There is no Coupon entity in the model (PromoBanner.couponCode is a free string on a banner), coupons are applied in the cart, and the field is read by nothing. The catalogue can only DECLARE policy: rename to `couponPolicy: "allow" | "block"`, publish it on every ResolvedPrice, and state that the cart service enforces it. Precedence follows the same principle as row discounts — PERMANENT BEATS TEMPORARY: `CatalogCountryConfig.isCouponEligible === false` (per listing × country, already in the model at types/index.ts:964) is a hard block, and a sale's couponPolicy can only further RESTRICT, never grant. A sale that sets allow where isCouponEligible is false is a gap, not an override. Delete the UI copy at page.tsx:375 ("the customer gets whichever is better, not both") — that describes cart behaviour nothing here implements, and shipping the sentence is a lie about the system.

cases.case: A sale spanning a timezone boundary between UAE and KSA?
cases.behaviour: Broken twice today. (a) `timezone` is inert: the editor writes `new Date(e.target.value).toISOString()` from a datetime-local input (page.tsx:172,178), so the wall clock is read in the OPERATOR'S BROWSER zone — an ops person in Riyadh scheduling "Friday 00:00 Asia/Dubai" produces 01:00 Dubai, and nothing converts. (b) A single instant cannot express what a regional campaign means. FIX: store the naive wall clock plus a zone (SaleWindow) and derive the instant, never the reverse; add COUNTRY_TZ (no such map exists in the repo — the four zones are hardcoded SelectItems at page.tsx:186-189). Two modes, because both intents are real: `local` resolves the same wall clock in each country's own zone (four different instants — "48 hours from local midnight", Ramadan/Eid, the midnight drop; established decision 9 says the countries have their own clocks), `absolute` flips every country at one instant computed from the naive time in the declared timezone (a synchronised global drop). OTHERS has no zone and is selectable in the COUNTRIES array, so in local mode it falls back to the sale's declared `timezone` — stated, not left undefined. saleState becomes saleStateFor(sale, country, now): a sale is legitimately live in UAE and scheduled in KSA, which one SALE_STATE_META badge cannot show — the header shows a per-country strip. `now` must come from the server; page.tsx:94 calls saleState(sale) with no argument inside a client component, making a pricing decision depend on the customer's clock.

cases.case: Inventory-limited flash sales ("first 100 units")?
cases.behaviour: Supported as a DECLARATION, never as a counter in the CMS — this is an ownership boundary and I am deciding it rather than leaving it open. A units-remaining number is a strongly-consistent decrementing resource; holding it in a read-mostly cacheable content service means either making the CMS transactional or overselling under concurrency and showing "42 left at this price" that is wrong. So: the catalogue declares SaleBudget { kind: "units" | "orders" | "spend"; limit; scope: "sale" | "per_unit"; perCustomerMax? } as part of the published sale contract; the ORDER SERVICE enforces it at checkout; the CMS displays consumption as read-only telemetry read back from that service and never stores it. resolveUnitPrice takes budget state as an INPUT (ctx.budgetOpen(saleId)) and marks the result `volatile: true`, which is the flag that shortens the cache TTL — and the reason to keep budgeted sales rare. Do not repurpose RegionalData.warehouseStock: that is per-country fulfilment stock, the only stock number in the model, and confusing it with a campaign budget would make a sale end when a warehouse restocks.

cases.case: Per-city sales?
cases.behaviour: Supported, by adding `cityId?` to FlashSaleRule. This is currently impossible and the omission is inconsistent with the rest of the model: two of the three price homes are already country+city (DiagnosticsServicePrice, TreatmentPlanPrice), so you can set a Dubai price for an IV plan but cannot discount it in Dubai only. Resolution order city rule → country rule → none, using the SlotGroup precedent already in the product (a row with no cityId is the national fallback, `groups.filter(g => !g.cityId || g.cityId === k.cityId)`, DiagnosticsSlots.tsx:392) so it reads as one system. Two constraints: the merge uses mergeOverride inherit semantics (undefined means inherit, not zero) and not the bare spread; and Listing.priceFloors stays COUNTRY-level and binds city-scoped rules too, so a city rule cannot silently escape the listing's floor. Cities come from the existing 7-row City master; OTHERS has no city, so a city rule on OTHERS is a gap.

cases.case: A sale on a combo whose parts are individually on sale?
cases.behaviour: The combo price stands; a sale on a part does NOT flow into the combo. A combo is its own PricedUnit (kind: "combo") with its own standingPrice, not a computed sum — so it resolves independently, exactly like any other unit. The reason is threefold: a sum-of-parts combo would double-discount (combo saving plus part sale), it can fall below the combo's own floor with no floor able to catch it, and it makes the combo's price uncacheable because it depends on N other listings' sale state. Add a gap check that warns when one live sale covers both a combo and its components, because that is nearly always an authoring mistake. NOTE the modelling gap: there is no combo on Listing at all — `Bundle` exists only on `Product` with five hardcoded country columns (bundlePriceUae/Ksa/Qatar/Kuwait/Others + compareAtBundlePrice), which must not be carried over; a combo's rows are PricedRow[] like every other unit. Whether the customer should get min(combo price, sum of sale-priced parts) is a commercial call, not an engineering one — see open questions.

cases.case: Sales on subscriptions/programs where the discount applies to which cycles?
cases.behaviour: SUBSCRIPTIONS: a sale must declare cycle scope or it is a standing revenue risk — "40% off" on a monthly subscription forever is a different business from 40% off cycle one. Add `subscriptionScope: "first_cycle" | "all_cycles_while_live" | "fixed_cycles"` + `cycles?`, DEFAULT "first_cycle" because it is the only option that cannot accidentally give away margin in perpetuity. "all_cycles_while_live" means what the overlay model implies: the discount stops at the window close even for an active subscriber, and the next renewal bills at standingPrice. The catalogue publishes the cycle scope and the locked price for the cycles it covers; the order service bills renewals. Also a cleanup this exposes: SubscriptionPlan.finalPrice and .discountPct (types/index.ts:763-771) are hand-typed duplicates of derived values — precisely the pattern established decision 5 forbids, the one that produced the 100-biomarker claim on a 70-marker panel — and must be derived from RegionalData.subscriptionPrice* and subscriptionDiscountPct. PROGRAMS: a sale cannot target a Journey, and should not. Journeys carry no price (PageBlockConfig.priceLabel is a display string, "From AED 899/mo" on jr-weightloss); sales target priced units, journeys are context wrappers. But priceLabel then goes stale the moment a sale opens — derive it from min(sellingPrice) across the journey's listings' units, or keep it as a manual override that a gap check flags when it disagrees.

cases.case: How does an ops person see "what is this customer paying right now and why"?
cases.behaviour: Today: impossible. No function takes a Listing and returns its priced units with a sale applied, for any department; the only surface is a 6-row preview, hardcoded UAE, hardcoded variants[0], which prints "no UAE price to show" for every Diagnostics and Treatments listing. FIX: one engine (explainPrice, sharing code with resolveUnitPrice so the two can never disagree) surfaced in three places. (1) A "Price explain" drawer in the listing editor, per unit per country per city, showing which price row won and which fields it inherited, the standing discount, every candidate sale with its computed result and why it did or did not win, the floor and which floor bound (rule vs priceFloors), budget state, coupon policy, final. (2) The flash-sale preview replaced by a real per-unit × per-country matrix instead of one hardcoded column. (3) An Administration → Price Inspector: listing + country + city + `asAt` timestamp, which is what makes a support ticket answerable ("they say they saw 640 at 11pm yesterday"). IMPORTANT LIMIT: `asAt` cannot read the sale store, which holds only current state — it must reconstruct the sale set by replaying AuditLogEntry.changes, which is feasible because entries carry timestamp plus before/after (established decision 10). That is only usable if the sale editor stops patching per keystroke: today every character in a discount field calls patch() (page.tsx:352-356), which floods the audit log for what the page itself calls "the highest-risk edit in the CMS". The editor needs commit-on-blur or an explicit save. Each PriceStep also carries auditEntryId, linking the price shown to the edit that caused it.

cases.case: Does the read path stay cacheable if prices are resolved per request?
cases.behaviour: Yes, and the current design is right not to write onto listings — but the mechanism is unstated and needs to be. Resolution is a pure function of (listing snapshot, sale set snapshot, country, cityId, instant), and the only volatile input is the clock. So the resolver returns `revalidateAt`: the next instant at which any answer could change — min over the next sale start, the next sale end (both resolved IN THE PER-COUNTRY ZONE, which is why SaleWindow matters here too) and the next PriceChange.effectiveAt. That converts "resolve per request" into "cache until the next boundary": long TTL between events, hard flip at the boundary, no cron job, no stale discount. Cache key is (listingId, country, cityId, locale); tag-based invalidation on listing edit and on any sale edit whose scope resolves to the listing. Budget-limited sales are the single exception — `volatile: true` forces a short TTL or a client-side budget check, which is a further reason to keep budgets rare. Two rules that follow: the resolver must take `now` from the server rather than calling new Date() in a component (page.tsx:94 does the latter today), and nothing may be persisted onto the listing by a sale, or the cache key stops describing the answer.

cases.case: Should there be a scheduled price CHANGE (permanent) distinct from a time-boxed SALE?
cases.behaviour: Yes — it is the missing entity, and the distinction is mechanical rather than cosmetic. A SALE is a read-path overlay that expires and never writes. A PRICE CHANGE writes the new standingPrice at effectiveAt, snapshots the previous prices, and records before/after in the audit log with a stated reason. Without it, every permanent repricing is a hand-edit at some unrecorded moment with no schedule, no reason and no rollback path; and worse, ops will use a long flash sale as a price change, which means every sale someone forgets to end silently becomes the price — the exact legacy failure that the flash-sales page's own amber card describes. Having both makes the misuse detectable: a gap check flags a sale whose window exceeds N days with "should this be a PriceChange?", and a PriceChange whose reason is a campaign name is equally suspect in reverse. PriceChange reuses the naive-local + timezone rule from SaleWindow, targets PricedUnitRefs (so it works identically across all three price homes), and adds "priceChange" to AuditEntityType. This is genuinely new scope — a new entity, a new store, a new page, and an apply step — and should be sequenced after the PricedUnit adapter, which it depends on.

cases.case: EXTRA — Does a flash sale apply on top of a partner-contracted price?
cases.behaviour: No, by default. PartnerPrice { variantId?, country?, cityId?, price, discountType?, discountValue? } is a contracted number and is the only pattern in the model with three optional scoping axes; when one resolves for (partnerId, unit, country, city) it IS the standingPrice, and resolveUnitPrice returns { kind: "excluded", reason: "partner_contracted" } for the sale. FlashSale.appliesToPartnerPricing is typed as the literal `false` so widening it is a deliberate change, not an accident. NOTE that PartnerPrice has no resolver at all today — it is edited in PartnerAccessSection.tsx:168-178 and read by nothing — so the PricedUnit adapter is also where partner pricing finally becomes resolvable, and it uses "percentage" where FlashSaleRule uses "percent" (the enum drift DiscountKind fixes).

cases.case: EXTRA — How does a sale interact with the row-level discountType/discountValue already on DiagnosticsServicePrice and TreatmentPlanPrice?
cases.behaviour: This is the largest correctness hole and the three-number contract closes it. Every priced unit resolves to listPrice (the marketing anchor: compareAtPrice | retailPrice | compareAtPriceOverride), standingPrice (what it sells for absent any sale — the OUTPUT of finalPlanPrice / finalServicePrice, i.e. the row discount is already inside it), and sellingPrice (standingPrice with at most one sale). Rules: a sale operates on standingPrice, never on listPrice; a sale NEVER compounds with the row discount, because the row discount is already inside standingPrice; strike-through shows listPrice when listPrice > sellingPrice, else standingPrice; the displayed discount % is always derived against whichever number is struck (established decision 5). The justification is the same permanent-beats-temporary principle used for coupons: the row discount lives on the listing and survives, so it is part of the permanent price. Today none of this is decided — the single effectivePrice call site passes RAW regionalData[].price and never passes the other two homes at all, so a Treatments plan's row discount and a flash sale have never met. One UI consequence: relabel the row-level discount as "standing discount (permanent)" in TreatmentPlans.tsx and DiagnosticsSlots.tsx, so ops stop reaching for it to run campaigns — that misuse is how "50% OFF" became a permanent category in the legacy catalogue.

cases.case: EXTRA — Is per-unit exclusion needed, given Listing.discountable is a listing-wide boolean?
cases.behaviour: Yes, from two directions, and they are different things. REGULATORY/PERMANENT stays on the listing: Listing.discountable === false is the blunt permanent gate (GLP-1, MOH-regulated, partner-contracted), and it should be DERIVED-or-warned from ListingAttributes.medicineType and isRxRequired rather than left purely hand-set, since an Rx item that someone forgot to mark is a compliance incident and not a merchandising slip. MERCHANDISING/TEMPORARY goes on the sale: SaleScope.excludedUnitRefs, so "the whole campaign tag except the 8-session course" needs no listing edit to launch and leaves no residue when the window closes — the same argument that justifies the sale entity existing. ResolvedPrice distinguishes the reasons (listing_not_discountable / unit_excluded_by_sale / partner_contracted / rx_or_regulated) because "why is this not discounted" is half of what Price Explain must answer, and the amber "N in scope cannot be discounted" banner (page.tsx:394-402) currently collapses all of them into one sentence.

cases.case: EXTRA — Does the sale's landing page actually work?
cases.behaviour: No — the best idea in the design has no implementation, and it belongs in the critique rather than on the keep-list. The type comment (types/index.ts:241-244) and the UI (page.tsx:156-159) both claim "the sale only drives its MEMBERSHIP, so it fills while the window is open and empties when it closes", but landingCategoryId is written at page.tsx:145, gap-checked at flash-sales.ts:102, defaulted at api.ts:2027 and read by NOTHING: Category has no listingIds and membership flows from Listing.subCategoryIds ∩ Category.subCategoryIds. KEEP the idea loudly — reusing a real category page is what stops a discount becoming a taxonomy node (established decision 2), and it gives merchandisers the hero, SEO and surface tools they already know — but it owes a resolver: categoryMembers(categoryId, listings, sales, now) unioning static members with the resolved scope of every live sale pointing at that category. Without it, launching a sale produces an empty landing page, and the gap check that demands a landing page is enforcing a link to nothing.

risks: Field renames break audit silently, with no type error: api.ts:2047 enumerates audited fields as string literals ("tagId", "pricedUnit", "stacksWithCoupons", "landingSlug", …). Dropping pricedUnit/stacksWithCoupons and replacing startsAt/endsAt/timezone/scopeKind with window/scope means those edits stop being recorded while everything still compiles — and audit replay is what Price Inspector's `asAt` depends on. The audited-field list must become a typed keyof FlashSale array, not strings.

Three seed/default sites must move together or the prototype shows nonsense: seedFlashSales() (api.ts:989-1016), createFlashSale defaults (api.ts:2012-2030), and the cloneSale deep-copy. fs-weekend is deliberately seeded as the broken case (pricedUnit "service_option" over two listings with variants: []), so it should be re-seeded as the case that now WORKS, to demonstrate the fix rather than the bug.

The PricedUnit adapter changes the activation gate's meaning, and the gate is currently wrong in both directions: listingActivationRequirements (catalogue.ts:85-117) checks hasPricedVariant ungated by department, so l-blood (priced service options) and l-iv (four priced plans) FAIL the price requirement while seeded active, and the 35 sd-tx-injection listings PASS on regionalData[].price the editor hides for tx. Once pricedUnitsFor(l) exists the gate should ask "≥1 priced unit for ≥1 enabled country" — but that reclassifies existing seed data and may block listings ops currently sees as fine. Sequence it as a deliberate follow-up, not a side effect.

356 MIGRATED_LISTINGS carry variants[].regionalData[].price and 35 of them are department: "treatments" on subDepartmentId "sd-tx-injection" — an id referenced but never defined (MIGRATED_SUBDEPARTMENTS is []). The adapter will surface that money as variant units on Treatments listings, contradicting decision 3. Either the adapter refuses variant units for tx (and the money stays unreachable, as today), or those 35 need migrating to TreatmentPlan.pricing. Migration is the right answer but it is data work, not type work.

schema-map.ts has no row at all for DiagnosticsServiceOption.pricing or TreatmentPlan.pricing — the two newer priced units have no declared DB mapping, while catalog_pricing already carries city_id and retail_price. Every new field here (FlashSaleRule.cityId, SaleBudget, PriceChange) extends a surface that is already behind, so the schema-map rows should be added in the same change or the gap compounds.

Per-keystroke patch() in the flash-sales editor (page.tsx:139-140, 352-362) writes an audit entry per character. Combined with `asAt` replay this is not just noise — it makes the audit log the slowest possible way to reconstruct a sale. Commit-on-blur or explicit save is a prerequisite for Price Inspector, not a polish item.

Timezone correctness needs a real IANA conversion (Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone, or a date library). Hand-rolling UTC offsets will be wrong across a DST-observing OTHERS market even though none of UAE/KSA/Qatar/Kuwait observe DST — the bug will not appear in the four seeded countries and will ship undetected.

mergeOverride fixes a live bug, which means resolved prices will CHANGE for any listing whose city row has a cleared field — today those units read as unpriced. That is the correct behaviour but it is a visible price movement in the prototype and should be called out rather than landing quietly.

Scope: PricedUnit adapter + resolution + explain + gap rewrite is one coherent change. PriceChange is a second entity with its own store, page and apply step, and Price Inspector's `asAt` depends on audit replay. Shipping all three at once risks the adapter (the load-bearing part) being reviewed as an afterthought.
openQuestions: COMBO: when a combo's components are individually on sale, does the customer get min(combo standingPrice, sum of components' sellingPrice)? Recommend NO — combo price stands. Needs commercial sign-off because it is a visible "cheaper to buy the parts" moment.
PARTNER: does a flash sale ever apply on top of a resolved PartnerPrice? Recommend NO — contracted price wins. One yes/no per partner contract type, or one global no.

SUBSCRIPTION: with subscriptionScope "all_cycles_while_live", does an already-subscribed customer's next renewal after the window closes bill at standingPrice? Recommend YES (the overlay expires for everyone). Alternative is a locked-in cohort price, which the catalogue cannot express and the order service would have to own.

FIXED DISCOUNTS: block a fixed-amount rule on a tag scope spanning more than one department outright, or allow it with a mandatory floorPrice per country? Need one answer — the guard is written either way.
SALE DURATION: what window length trips the "should this be a PriceChange?" gap — 30 days? Needs one number.

REGULATED ITEMS: should discountable be FORCED to false (not merely warned) for listings whose ListingAttributes.medicineType is a prescription class or isRxRequired is true? Yes/no; if yes, the field becomes derived and the editor control disappears for those listings.

BUDGET TELEMETRY: will the Order Service expose a read endpoint for sale consumption (units/orders/spend by saleId)? Yes/no — if no, SaleBudget ships as a declaration with no consumption display in the CMS.

CATEGORY MEMBERSHIP: when a live sale injects listings into its landing category, do those listings also appear in that category's normal browse and search results, or only on the campaign page? One answer — it decides whether categoryMembers has one mode or two.

cases.case: WHERE A COMBO LIVES (the core decision)
cases.behaviour: A combo is its OWN Listing carrying `combo?: ComboConfig` — the exact pattern already used by `diagnostics?: DiagnosticsConfig` and `treatments?: TreatmentsConfig`. NOT variant-level (a variant is one combination of axes on ONE listing and cannot reference another listing's plan or service option). NOT 'a listing referencing listings' (a listing is not priced — its variants/options/plans are). The components reference PRICED UNITS via `PricedUnitRef`. Being a Listing buys, for free and with zero new machinery: own URL + slug, the four states, `countryConfig`, `tagIds` (so flash-sale scope works), `subCategoryIds` placement, SEO locales, `priceFloors`, `partnerAccess`, `journeyIds`, PDP, and audit as `AuditEntityType: "listing"`. No new store: combos live in `LISTINGS_STORE`. No sixth department, no new taxonomy node.

cases.case: The combo's own department / sub-department
cases.behaviour: Derived from the ANCHOR component, never free-chosen: `listing.department` and `listing.subDepartmentId` = the anchor part's. A combo spanning departments is still 'one thing' for classification, and the anchor is the clinically dominant part (blood panel in 'Blood panel + GLP-1 + coach'). Enforces decision 2 (Department = WHAT IT IS, 1 per listing) and gives Zoho a default book. Exactly one component must have `isAnchor: true` → ActivationRequirement `comboAnchor` (BLOCKS publish). Combos are placed in Category→Sub-category like anything else; 'Bundles' is a CATEGORY, never a sub-department.

cases.case: Fixed-price combo
cases.behaviour: `priceMode: "fixed"`. Money lives on `ComboConfig.pricing: ComboPrice[]` — the same Pattern A row (country + optional cityId) as `DiagnosticsServicePrice` / `TreatmentPlanPrice`, so combos are the fourth home for price and reuse the shape rather than inventing a fifth. `compareAtPrice` is NOT typed by hand: it is DERIVED as `sumOfParts(country, cityId)` (decision 5 — the hand-typed compare-at is exactly how '100 biomarkers on a 70-marker panel' happened). BLOCKS publish: every country with a `CatalogCountryConfig` row must have a resolvable `ComboPrice.price > 0` (ActivationRequirement `comboPriced`, mirroring `diagnosticsGaps`' per-country priced-option rule but promoted to a real gate).

cases.case: Sum-of-parts combo
cases.behaviour: `priceMode: "sum_of_parts"`. NOTHING is stored. Price = `Σ unitPrice(c.ref, country, cityId) × c.quantity` over non-freebie components. This is the 'convenience bundle, no discount' baseline. Publishable with zero `ComboPrice` rows. Degrades gracefully as parts reprice — that is the point. Compare-at is suppressed (no saving to show); `showCompareAtPrice` is forced false on the combo PDP.

cases.case: Percentage-off-sum combo
cases.behaviour: `priceMode: "percent_off_sum"`, `ComboPrice.discountValue` = percent per country (city override allowed). Price = `round2(sum × (1 − pct/100))`, then clamped up to `max(ComboPrice.floorPrice, listing.priceFloors[country].amount)` — reusing the existing floor field so combos inherit floor semantics from flash sales verbatim. `discountValue >= 100` BLOCKS publish (same rule as `flashSaleGaps`). A fourth mode `fixed_off_sum` (absolute amount off the sum) is supported by the same row via `discountValue` + `discountType: "percent"|"fixed"` — note the enum must be `"percent"`, matching `FlashSaleRule`/`DiagnosticsServicePrice`/`TreatmentPlanPrice`, NOT the `"percentage"` drift on `PromoBanner`/`heroDiscountType`/`PartnerPrice`.

cases.case: Per-country pricing
cases.behaviour: `fixed`: one `ComboPrice` row per country, plus the combo's own `countryConfig` row (no row = not sold there, Pattern B). Derived modes: per-country automatically, because each part's own resolver is per-country. A combo's SELLABLE countries = intersection of the non-substitutable components' available countries ∩ the combo's own `countryConfig` rows. `comboCountryReadiness()` derives this; the operator's `countryConfig` row is an INTENT and the resolver says whether it is satisfiable. A country row whose intersection is empty is an ActivationRequirement failure (BLOCKS publish for the whole combo — one dead country row is a mistake, not a graceful state).

cases.case: Per-city pricing
cases.behaviour: `fixed`: `ComboPrice.cityId` set = city override, resolved by `comboPrice(cfg, country, cityId)` using effectiveSlot's INHERIT-NOT-ZERO merge (`Object.keys(city).forEach(k => city[k] === undefined && (merged[k] = base[k]))`), NOT the bare spread used by `servicePrice`/`planPrice` — those two carry a live bug where clearing a typed city price writes an own `undefined` property that overwrites the country price, killing `finalPlanPrice`/`finalServicePrice` at their `p.price === undefined` guard. Derived modes: city flows from each part via `unitPrice(ref, country, cityId)`. Only 7 cities exist and `OTHERS` has none, so a city override with no matching `City` row is an advisory gap, not a blocker.

cases.case: THE MISSING RESOLVER — one function that finds a base price for any priced unit
cases.behaviour: `unitPrice(ref: PricedUnitRef, listings: Listing[], country, cityId?): number | undefined` in a new `src/lib/pricing.ts`, dispatching: `variant` → new `variantPrice(v, country, cityId)` (finally gives `RegionalData.cityPrices` its first resolver — today it has 2 references repo-wide and no editor), `service_option` → `finalServicePrice(servicePrice(opt, country, cityId))`, `plan` → `finalPlanPrice(planPrice(plan, country, cityId), cfg.dripSpeed, cfg.slowDripSurcharge)`. Combos force into existence the function the codebase does not have for ANY department. Second payoff: `flash-sales/page.tsx:405` replaces `l.variants?.[0]?.regionalData?.find(r => r.country === "UAE")?.price` with `unitPrice()` per `FlashSale.pricedUnit`, which is how the inert `pricedUnit` field gets its first reader and how `fs-weekend` (pricedUnit `service_option`, scoped to two Diagnostics listings with `variants: []`) stops rendering literally 'no UAE price to show'.

cases.case: ACTIVATION GATE — must change, or no combo can ever be published
cases.behaviour: `listingActivationRequirements` (src/lib/catalogue.ts:85-117) is ungated by department and requires `hasPricedVariant` on `variants[].regionalData[].price`. A combo has `variants: []`, so `disabled={st.id === "active" && unmetReqs.length > 0}` (listings/[id]/page.tsx:699) and the hard block at line 647 make Published unreachable. Replace the `variant` row with `{ key: "pricedUnit", label: "At least one priced sellable unit", met: hasPricedUnit(l) }` dispatching on department: products→variant price, diagnostics→priced active service option, treatments→priced active plan, combo→resolvable combo price. This ALSO fixes the pre-existing bug where seeded `l-blood` (Standard 899 / Fast Track 1099) and `l-iv` (four priced plans) sit at `status: "active"` while failing the gate. The `image` requirement stays and is NOT satisfied by composing part images: a combo must have its own `mediaGallery` hero (BLOCKS publish) — a PDP whose hero is a collage of three unrelated part photos reads as broken.

cases.case: WHERE 'BLOCKS PUBLISH' HAS TO LIVE (mechanism, not verdict)
cases.behaviour: The repo has a hard split that must be respected: `diagnosticsGaps`/`treatmentsGaps` are ADVISORY — wired only to section `hasError` flags and panels, and `unmetReqs` never includes them (their own comments say 'Deliberately separate'). So every case labelled BLOCKS below is implemented as an `ActivationRequirement` row appended when `l.combo` is present (mirroring how matrix-mode appends `comboUnique`/`comboComplete`). Everything labelled DEGRADES goes in a new advisory `comboGaps(l, listings)` wired to the `combo` section's `hasError`. Putting a blocker in `comboGaps` would silently not block.

cases.case: A part goes out of stock
cases.behaviour: DEGRADES GRACEFULLY. Never blocks publish (stock is a runtime fact, not a publish fact) and never changes status. Derived: `comboStock(cfg, listings, country) = min over variant components of floor(regionalData.warehouseStock / quantity)`; service_option and plan components contribute `Infinity` because they are capacity-booked against a `SlotGroup`, not stocked. Zero → PDP shows the combo out of stock exactly as a variant does, honouring `showStockIndicator`. A variant component whose `RegionalData.isAvailable === false` in a country removes that country from the sellable intersection at runtime (derived, no edit).

cases.case: A part is Inactive (URL live, delisted)
cases.behaviour: DEGRADES GRACEFULLY — the combo keeps selling. `inactive` means removed from browse, not unsellable; the URL still resolves and existing links keep working, so a part that is delisted-but-live is a perfectly legitimate combo member (this is in fact the cleanest way to sell something ONLY inside a combo). Advisory gap on the combo so the operator sees it, because delisting is usually a step toward retirement.

cases.case: A part is Archived (retired) or still Draft
cases.behaviour: BLOCKS PUBLISH: an ActivationRequirement `comboPartsLive` requiring every non-substitutable component's listing to be `active` or `inactive`. Both `draft` and `archived` have a dead URL — you cannot sell what does not resolve. RUNTIME, on a LIVE combo whose part is archived after the fact: if the component is `substitutable` with a live `substituteRefs` entry, resolve to the substitute, write an audit entry with actor 'system', and carry on. Otherwise the combo is auto-forced to `inactive` (URL live, out of browse) with a system audit entry — never `archived`, never deleted (decision 4: nothing deletes; retire = deactivate). Deriving downward is the invariant: a combo may never be more live than its parts.

cases.case: A part is not sold in one country
cases.behaviour: Two sub-cases. (1) The component is `substitutable: false` → that country drops out of the combo's sellable intersection. If the operator has a `countryConfig` row for it, that is an ActivationRequirement failure (BLOCKS — the row is a lie). If they have no row, nothing to fix: no row = not available, Pattern B, works already. (2) `substitutable: true` and `isFreebie` or has a country-valid `substituteRefs` entry → the combo sells in that country with the reduced/substituted set; derived modes recompute the sum from what actually ships, so the price self-corrects with no edit. DEGRADES. Per-country component sets are the norm here, not an edge case — 19 of 32 cross-country diagnostics packages already carry different marker sets per country.

cases.case: Parts with different fulfilment paths → the order splits
cases.behaviour: One cart line, one payment, N fulfilment jobs created at order time — one per component (blood draw, shipped medicine, booked consult). `Listing.fulfilmentPath` stays a required scalar and is set to the ANCHOR's path (1,559 seeded listings carry it as a scalar; widening it to an array breaks them and the activation gate). The truth is DERIVED: `comboFulfilmentPaths(cfg, listings): FulfilmentPath[]`, the distinct set, which is what the order service splits on. Ordering matters clinically, so reuse the EXISTING vocabulary rather than invent a second one: `ComboComponent.dependsOnComponentId?: string` + `gating?: ProtocolGating` (`"none"|"lab_result"|"consultation_approval"|"prescription"`) + `gatingNote?`, and `ComboConfig.sequencing: "parallel" | "gated"`. 'Blood panel → coach reads your results' is `gating: "lab_result"`. A dependency cycle BLOCKS publish. The `Order` type in this repo is a thin mock (`items: Array<{name;type}>`), so the CMS's job is to DECLARE the split shape, not implement it — say so rather than pretending the order service is modelled.

cases.case: A part is Rx-gated
cases.behaviour: DEGRADES — publishable, with the gate. `comboRequiresRx(cfg, listings)` = any component listing's `attributes.isRxRequired`. DERIVED, never hand-set on the combo (a hand-set false over an Rx part is a compliance hole). Consequence: the whole combo inherits the prescription gate — PDP shows it, checkout enforces it, and `gating: "prescription"` is auto-implied on that component. Same derivation for `requiresConsultation`. A combo cannot be LESS gated than its strictest part.

cases.case: A part is a controlled substance
cases.behaviour: BLOCKS PUBLISH unconditionally in the prototype, with an explicit 'needs a human decision' message rather than an invented policy. `attributes.isControlledSubstance` on any component → the combo cannot be published until Regulatory signs off; whether Valeo may bundle a controlled substance at all is a legal question the CMS must not answer by default. Modelled as an ActivationRequirement plus an override field (`ComboConfig.controlledSubstanceApprovedBy?: string` + `approvalNote`) so the sign-off is auditable rather than a silent toggle.

cases.case: A part is non-discountable (the GLP-1 back door)
cases.behaviour: BLOCKS PUBLISH for the discounting modes. `Listing.discountable === false` is documented as PERMANENT truth (GLP-1, MOH-regulated, partner-contracted). Two rules: (a) `priceMode` of `percent_off_sum`/`fixed_off_sum` with ANY non-discountable component → BLOCKS. (b) `priceMode: "fixed"` where the combo price is below `Σ list price of the non-discountable components` in any country → BLOCKS. Without (b) a fixed-price combo discounts an undiscountable item through the back door, which is the single most dangerous thing combos enable. `sum_of_parts` is always allowed. Separately, the combo's OWN discountability must NOT be stored: `activeSalesFor` reads the stored `l.discountable`, and a stored derived value goes stale the moment a part later becomes non-discountable — so call sites pass `activeSalesFor({ ...l, discountable: comboDiscountable(cfg, listings) }, sales, country)`.

cases.case: A part is already inside a flash sale
cases.behaviour: DEGRADES, with a determinism rule and a suppression rule. RULE: a combo's price is computed from the LIST prices of its parts, never from sale-applied prices, and a flash sale applies to the combo only if the COMBO LISTING is itself in scope (by its own `tagIds` or `listingIds`). Otherwise `percent_off_sum` stacks on a part's 40% flash and prints negative margin, and the PDP price changes mid-window with nobody editing anything. SECOND HALF: tag-scoped sales match component listings independently, so a part can be 40% off standalone while the combo advertises 'save AED 200' and is genuinely WORSE than buying separately. `comboIsWorseThanParts(cfg, listings, sales, country)` compares the combo's effective price against `Σ` the parts' EFFECTIVE (sale-applied) prices; when true, suppress the combo from browse in that country and warn the operator. Does not block publish — sales come and go, and unpublishing on a transient window is worse than hiding.

cases.case: VAT / Zoho when parts route to DIFFERENT invoicing entities
cases.behaviour: The combo gets NO book of its own. `SubDepartmentCountryConfig.zohoBook` is per sub-department × country with `overrides` keyed on `medicineClass`, so a UAE combo of blood panel (dmcc) + GLP-1 (shifa, zero-rated) + coach consult (dmcc) is one payment across two books. Invoicing is PER COMPONENT, allocated out of the single customer-facing price. `ComboConfig.allocationBasis: "pro_rata_list" | "explicit"`, default `pro_rata_list`: each component's share = its list price in that country ÷ the sum, with LARGEST-REMAINDER rounding so the allocated lines sum EXACTLY to the charged amount (a 0.01 discrepancy against a settled payment is a finance incident). `"explicit"` exists for the cases where pro-rata puts the wrong revenue in the wrong entity: `ComboComponent.allocationShare?: { country: Country; pct: number }[]`, and shares not summing to 100 per country BLOCK publish. VAT is then computed per allocated line at that component's own sub-department × country rate, so a mixed 0%/5% combo invoices correctly. Zoho ids stay where they are (`RegionalData.zohoId` per variant × country) — the combo mints none.

cases.case: vatMode mismatch across components in one country
cases.behaviour: BLOCKS PUBLISH for that country. `SubDepartmentCountryConfig.vatMode` is `"exclusive" | "inclusive"` per sub-department × country. If two components in the same country disagree, one displayed number cannot yield a defensible tax base — half the price includes VAT and half does not, and no allocation can recover it. Differing RATES with a uniform mode is fine (allocate, then apply each rate). This is the one VAT case that is a hard gate rather than a warning.

cases.case: Qatar
cases.behaviour: DEGRADES. `invoicingEnabled: false` means Qatar creates no invoices at all, for combos exactly as for anything else. Combos are sellable and priceable in Qatar; the allocation is computed and recorded for reporting but no Zoho document is produced. Do not block, do not special-case the price. (Whether Qatar combos are commercially permitted is listed as an open question — but the CMS default is 'works, no invoice'.)

cases.case: The combo's own SKU
cases.behaviour: NO new SKU for the whole. `ComboConfig.comboCode: string` — an operator-facing code, following the `Protocol.code` precedent, unique across combos (duplicate BLOCKS publish). Every component keeps its own `RegionalData.sku` and `zohoId` on the order and the invoice line. Rationale: a combo-level SKU implies a kitted, stock-held assembly, and Valeo assembles nothing — parts ship from their own warehouse and services are booked against slot groups. Minting one would create a second identity for stock, Zoho and the WMS to disagree about.

cases.case: The combo's own stock
cases.behaviour: NONE stored, fully derived (decision 5). `comboStock()` as above: min over variant components of `floor(warehouseStock / quantity)`, services contribute `Infinity`. A stored combo stock number is guaranteed to drift the first time a component sells standalone, which it will, because components remain independently purchasable — that is the whole point of referencing priced units rather than copying them.

cases.case: What the PDP shows
cases.behaviour: Own hero (required) + own EN/AR copy + a 'What's included' list of component cards, each linking to that part's own PDP. Price block: one combo price + a DERIVED compare-at equal to the sum of parts' list prices, so 'You save AED X' can never go stale — this is the honest number and the reason compare-at is not hand-typed. Do NOT render each part's own strike-through inside its card (`showCompareAtPrice` suppressed per card): a discount shown inside a discount double-counts the saving, which is precisely the class of error decision 5 exists to prevent. Freebie components render as 'Included free', contribute 0 to the sum, and still fulfil. Turnaround/delivery shows the SLOWEST component (`max` of `effectiveSlot().reportDaysMax`, `deliveryConfig` times, plan `validityDays`) — a combo is ready when its last part is ready; showing the fastest is a promise the combo cannot keep. Fulfilment is shown as the honest multi-path story ('nurse visit + shipped + booked call'), derived from `comboFulfilmentPaths`. SEO: the combo has its own `seoLocales` per country × language and is canonical for itself; do NOT copy component body copy into the combo PDP (thin/duplicate content against the parts' own canonical pages).

cases.case: What happens to a live combo when a part's price changes
cases.behaviour: Split by mode, and be honest about where the audit lands. DERIVED modes (`sum_of_parts`, `percent_off_sum`, `fixed_off_sum`): the customer-facing price moves immediately with no combo edit. The audit entry belongs on the PART listing, where it already lands today with before/after — do NOT fabricate a combo audit entry for a change nobody made on the combo (that is a phantom diff, the thing `listingDefaults()` exists to prevent). The combo surfaces the movement as derived drift in its editor. `fixed` mode: the price does NOT move; the DERIVED compare-at does, so the advertised saving silently changes. `ComboConfig.sumAtPublish?: { country: Country; amount: number; capturedAt: string }[]` is a per-country watermark captured at publish — the one deliberate stored-derived exception, justified because cross-entity drift detection has no other cheap reference, and it is NEVER read into a price, only compared. Drift beyond `driftWarnPct` (default 15) raises an advisory gap; if the sum falls BELOW the fixed price the combo is now more expensive than its parts and is suppressed from browse per `comboIsWorseThanParts`. Never auto-unpublish on a price change.

cases.case: Nesting: a component that is itself a combo
cases.behaviour: BLOCKS PUBLISH. A `PricedUnitRef` may only point at a `variant`, `service_option` or `plan` — none of which a combo listing has — so nesting is already structurally impossible at the type level; the gate exists to catch a ref whose target listing has `combo` set. Nesting would make allocation, VAT mode, Rx derivation and fulfilment splitting recursive for no commercial gain.

cases.case: Self-reference and duplicate refs
cases.behaviour: Self-reference (a component whose `listingId` is the combo itself) BLOCKS PUBLISH. Two components with an identical `PricedUnitRef` are MERGED into one row with summed `quantity` on save (the forgiving choice — an operator adding the same thing twice means quantity 2), and `quantity < 1` BLOCKS. `quantity > 1` is permitted only for `kind: "variant"`; a plan or service option is bought once (a course of 8 sessions is already `sessionCount`, not quantity 8) — quantity > 1 on those BLOCKS publish.

cases.case: Zero or one component
cases.behaviour: BLOCKS PUBLISH: at least two components (`comboMinComponents`). A one-part 'combo' is a listing, and letting one exist creates a duplicate PDP competing with the part's own canonical URL for the same intent.

cases.case: Partner-priced components
cases.behaviour: DEGRADES with a documented limitation. `PartnerPrice { variantId?, country?, cityId?, price, discountType?, discountValue? }` has three optional scoping axes and NO resolver anywhere today. Until one exists, a combo containing a component under partner-contracted pricing must be `priceMode: "fixed"` with its own `PartnerAccessEntry.pricing` at combo level; derived modes over partner-priced parts raise an advisory gap because the sum would use public list prices and undercut the contract. `partnerExclusive` is derived upward: any partner-exclusive component makes the combo partner-exclusive (hidden from Valeo master search).

cases.case: Tags on a combo
cases.behaviour: Unchanged rules, no exception. The combo carries its own `tagIds` from the closed namespace enum; `campaign` tags are how a combo enters a flash sale; `ops`/`clinical` tags stay internal and never reach a storefront filter. Component tags do NOT propagate to the combo — a combo is not automatically 'goal: weight-loss' because one part is; that would pollute storefront filters with transitive noise.
